tasks.spec:
You are building ONE new module in a Python repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps; this task needs neither.

YOU OWN EXACTLY TWO FILES:
  1. server/pipeline/guest_assets.py   (create it)
  2. fix-summary.md                    (create it)

Touching any other file fails the check.

## What happened, and why this module exists

A guest recorded an episode today. On 2026-08-06 at 12:19 he had replied to the pre-recording ask with everything requested: his own bio in his own words, how to pronounce his name, his LinkedIn profile, his company page, his phone number, a booking link, and a headshot attached to the message.

On the morning of the recording, canonical state said photo_url null, title null, and six guest-supplied items still open. The prep document called him "Guest", said "Recording: Not Yet Scheduled", and where his biography should have been it carried a generated label: "[Guest type] Consultant/Exit Planning Advisor + former industry and M&A executive".

Nothing was missing. The loop asked a file instead of asking the guest, and then filled the hole with a description somebody generated.

The owner's rule, in his words: take the guest's exact bio, or if not the exact bio then the best bio available; everyone needs a bio, contact info and a headshot; and where we have none of it, go and find it.

## What to build

    def resolve_guest_assets(guest, *, mail_source=None, research=None, web_source=None, now=None) -> dict

`guest` is a dict with at least name and email. The three sources are injected and each may be None, meaning that source is unavailable.

    mail_source.messages_for(email) -> list of dicts:
        {"id", "at" (ISO), "direction": "inbound"|"outbound", "text", "attachments": [{"filename", "mime", "size"}]}
    research.for_guest(guest)       -> dict, e.g. {"bio": ..., "company_website": ...}
    web_source.lookup(guest)        -> dict, e.g. {"bio": ..., "headshot_url": ..., "links": [...]}

Return a dict with `assets`, `gaps`, and `coverage`.

An asset is a dict: kind ("bio" | "headshot" | "contact"), value, provenance (a short string naming WHERE it came from, and mentioning the guest when it came from the guest), exact (bool), evidence_ref, captured_at.

Authority order, highest first, per asset kind:
  1. what the GUEST sent in an inbound message — his bio text, his attached image, his links and phone;
  2. the research already attached to the episode;
  3. the web lookup.

## The rules the check enforces, and the reason for each

1. A GUEST'S OWN WORDS ARE USED VERBATIM OR NOT AT ALL. Do not tidy, shorten, re-wrap, strip a smiley, fix a long sentence, or merge his paragraph with researched or scraped text. A bio is read aloud on air and published under his name. If you cannot use it as sent, it does not get to be called his bio.

2. `exact` IS TRUE ONLY FOR WHAT THE GUEST HIMSELF SUPPLIED. A researched or scraped bio is legitimate material and a perfectly good fallback — it is only dangerous when it is allowed to wear his voice. Anything downstream must be able to tell the two apart, forever.

3. AN ASSET NO SOURCE HAS IS A NAMED GAP, never an empty string and never something you compose. Put the kind in `gaps` with a short reason. Inventing a biography for a real person is the worst thing this module could do; an empty field and an unsearched one must never look the same.

4. ONE UNREADABLE SOURCE DEGRADES ONLY ITSELF. If a source raises, record it in `coverage` as unreached with a one-line reason and carry on with the others. Never let a failure become an empty result. Never let a credential, URL or token into that reason.

5. Extracting the bio from a message is the hard part; be conservative. The guest introduces it in prose and the bio follows. When you cannot identify a bio with confidence, record a gap rather than guessing a span — a wrong span is a wrong bio, and a wrong bio is worse than none.

For the headshot, prefer an inbound image attachment (mime image/*), and carry its filename in the asset. For contact, gather what the guest supplied — profile links, company links, phone — and keep them all.

## What NOT to do

Do not fetch anything yourself. Do not import requests, urllib, google api clients, or read the network or the filesystem. Every source is injected; a default of None simply means that source is unavailable. The real mail, research and web adapters are wired in a later round and are not yours.

## Run the exact check until it prints PASS

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u21_guest_assets_check.py --worktree "$PWD"

It drives four cases: a guest who answered in full, a guest who never replied, nothing available anywhere, and a source that raises. Read the failure text; it quotes what was expected.

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of the check command. Under 'Risk' say what could still put words in a guest's mouth despite this module. Under 400 words.
tasks.verified: Drives the resolver with the guest's real reply, with silence, with nothing available anywhere, and with a source that raises. The guest's bio must come back byte-for-byte and marked exact; his attached headshot and his own links and phone must win over anything generated; a researched fallback must be produced but must never be marked exact or attributed to him; an asset no source has must appear as a named gap with no value invented; and a raising source must degrade only itself while leaving a coverage trace.
